outcome: Severe perinatal morbidity and mortality (seizures, assisted ventilation, severe birth trauma, and perinatal death)
Severe maternal morbidity and mortality (severe postpartum hemorrhage, cardiac complication, and maternal death)
cohort: 61,106 women in Canada with term singleton deliveries by operative delivery with prolonged second stage of labour between 2003 and 2013
finding: Among women with dystocia, forceps and vacuum deliveries were associated with higher rates of severe perinatal morbidity and mortality compared with Caesarean delivery, whereas vacuum delivery was associated with decreased rates of severe maternal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Forceps and vacuum delivery is associated with increased rates of severe perinatal morbidity and mortality compared with Caesarean delivery among women with dystocia, whereas vacuum delivery is associated with decreased rates of severe maternal morbidity and mortality.
